notes:
The Geomancer empyrean coat. The shape is a straight ladder with one three-way CHOICE in the middle, and the choice is the whole reading problem: bullets 5-18 are three parallel walkthroughs under their own '== ... Option ==' headings, not eighteen consecutive steps. Sylvie hands out exactly ONE of the three crystals, so step 5's evidence is an alt-list of all three and never an AND-list, and the three crag steps share a group so all three draw at once -- a strict ladder would mark the Crag of Holla at a player carrying the Mea crystal. They are group members and NOT optional, the Mandragora-Mad shape: an exclusive choice is still a ladder position, and marking them optional would skip the only markable rungs the middle of this quest has.

The big win here is that 'Ergon Locus' and 'Scalable Area' both resolve as real entities, so four rungs that a ??? reading would have thrown away keep their markers. The page is careful and so is this: bullet 2's target IS the Ergon Locus, but bullet 3's target is a DIFFERENT thing -- a bare ??? at the base of the cliff overhang 'beneath the ergon locus' -- and that one is recorded as ??? and loses its marker honestly rather than borrowing the locus's name. Bullet 3 is also split in two, because ascending the Scalable Area at (G/H-7) and checking the ??? at (H-6/7) are separate acts in separate places, and the first is the one that can carry a marker and the one the "Climbing" key item is for.

The three fights are ONE step. It is the same monster, Otherworldly Rimester, at three content levels, and its battlefield's zone depends on which crystal you took, so the step carries no zone -- the Waking the Beast shape. It also carries the only real inference in this quest: the page states the Pale azure cloth only under the La Theine option (bullet 8), and bullet 19 does NOT mention the cloth -- it says only that Sylvie hands over the Treatise. The inference that all three fights grant it therefore rests on the header's Item Reqs alone, which lists the cloth among the key items this quest requires. That is a reading, not page text, and the step is medium for it.

Fame 'Adoulin' is not one of the addon's nine regions and gates nothing; the raw is kept. 'Level: 99 Geomancer' is both gates. Bullets 6, 7, 12-16 are tactics, 10 and 17 are reward tables, 18 is the retry loop and 23 is the Conquest Tally cooldown -- none is a step. The 'For the Rest of the Set' section after the walkthrough is deliberately NOT read as steps: this quest's reward is the Azimuth Coat and it ends at bullet 22; commissioning the other four pieces from Helina is a separate ongoing errand with its own order-slip key items, and folding it in would put four rungs after the quest is already over.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 2: The page writes it 'the Ergon Locus ???' and Ergon Locus is a real resolvable entity, so this rung keeps a marker instead of being thrown away as a bare ???.
  step 3: cannot be written as an item at all, which is what items_partial says.
  step 4: This is a different entity from step 2's Ergon Locus and the page names it only '???', so it keeps its rung and loses its marker.
  step 9: one step for all three battlefields, so it carries no zone: which one you are in depends on the crystal you took.

steps.note: at the Waterfront by Waypoint #9, as Geomancer. The sub-bullets are flagging conditions carried over from Geomancer Relic Armor -- the Crystallized lifestream essence goes to Wescolina in THAT quest, not this one -- and they warn that a Kupon A-AF +3 cannot be used to skip it.
Northeast of bivouac #2; a cutscene.
First half of bullet 3: ascend here, near the NW side of the Hot Spring. The "Climbing" key item is what this needs, and the page's alternative die, Tractor, and Raise twice down from bivouac #5.
Second half of bullet 3: directly east of the Scalable Area, at the base of the cliff overhang BENEATH the ergon locus. Cutscene.

she offers three challenges and you leave with exactly ONE crystal, so these are alternatives and not an AND-list. Holla crystal of gales = the level 109 fight in La Theine Plateau, Dem crystal of dunes = 125 in Konschtat Highlands, and the BLANK option gives the Mea crystal of flames = 135 in Tahrongi Canyon.
Crag of Holla, underneath the Telepoint; the crystal is consumed. Level 109 solo fight: Geomancer need not be your main job, Trusts allowed and Fellows not, buffs and TP reset, 5-10 minutes.
Crag of Dem, underneath the Telepoint; the crystal is consumed. Level 125 solo fight: Trusts allowed, Fellows and other players not, buffs and TP reset, 3 minutes.

Crag of Mea, underneath the Telepoint; the crystal is consumed. Level 135 and Geomancers only -- neither Trusts nor Fellows -- buffs and TP reset, 3 minutes. Losing costs the crystal, and bullet 18 sends you back to Sylvie for another as often as you like, so a loss is a loop and not a dead end.

The same Otherworldly Rimester, a Ghost, at three content levels BRD songs (Victory March, Magic Finale, Massacre Elegy, Foe Requiem VII, Horde Lullaby II, and at 135 also Dragonfoe Mambo and Valor Minuet V) and Dark Sphere, Terror Touch, Fear Touch, Ectosmash, of which only Dark Sphere ignores shadows. Weak to magic bursts; the 135 version rotates its elemental weakness on no known pattern. MEDIUM because the Pale azure cloth is stated only under the La Theine option (bullet 8); bullet 19 does not mention it at all, so reading it as common to all three fights rests on the header's Item Reqs alone.
the cloth goes to her and you leave with the Treatise.

MEDIUM on the zone only: bullet 20 gives the grid (H-7) and no zone. Western Adoulin is read from context -- Sylvie is there and the page names Selbina outright one bullet later, when it does change zone -- so the zone is inferred rather than written.
inside the Weaver's Guild.

the NEXT GAME DAY, which nothing in the packets reports; 15,000 experience points and the Azimuth Coat. Bullet 23 -- a fresh crystal from Sylvie once per Conquest Tally -- is the repeat cooldown, not a rung.

notes:
Epeolatry, the Runefencer ergon weapon. The page is one walkthrough for two different things and the split matters: bullets 1-18 are the QUEST, and bullet 18's own sub-bullet says the quest moves to the completed log there. Bullets 19-30 are the weapon's remaining three upgrade parts. They are kept as ordinary rungs -- the page numbers them, the header's Reward is Epeolatry and not the Lexeme Blade, and each part ends in a resolvable key item -- but flagged, because a runtime that only marks live quests will never show them and a human may want them cut. Bullets 31-33 ('== Dropped Item ==', talk to Geosuke, pay Runje a million gil to re-forge a blade you dropped) are a recovery procedure and are NOT rungs; the page itself marks that gil figure unverified, and the whole page is in Category:Information Needed.

The Lexeme Blade is the one thing this quest cannot observe. res/items.lua holds THREE items all named literally 'Lexeme Blade' -- 20750/20751/20752, DMG 226/228/231, exactly the wiki's I/II/III -- so the bare name resolves to whichever one the index happened to keep and would be a silently wrong id, while writing the page's own 'Lexeme Blade I' resolves to nothing. The page's names are written deliberately: stage C will drop those entries and quarantine them where a human can see the gap and, if they want it, pin the three ids by hand. Worse, the blade appears at three stages, so a single shared name would also trip the duplicate-evidence gate and demote the whole quest. What carries the ladder instead are the three Superlative runic rings (key items 2574/2575/2576), one per part, which resolve cleanly and are obtained exactly where the evidence says.

Smaller judgements. Bullets 19+20, 23+24 and 27+28 each merge: they are the blade and then the materials handed to the same Runje Desaali in one visit, so they are one rung with one AND-list, and merging keeps the readiness list honest. The battlefield door is named nowhere -- 'the door behind Yeggha Dolashi' -- so that step carries no target at all rather than borrowing Yeggha Dolashi, who is a bystander standing in front of it and resolves perfectly well, which is exactly the trap. Trades to Runje are CUMULATIVE, so a requirement of 9,999 High-Purity Bayld will read unmet by someone who has already deposited 9,000; the counts are still recorded, since they are what the page says and they add to the header's 13,099. 'All Coalitions Legend Rank' has no slot and no observable predicate. 'Must be on Runefencer' appears only against the battlefield and never in the header, so gates.jobs stays EMPTY: gating the whole quest to RUN off one line in a sub-bullet is the mistake the guide warns about, and it would hide the quest from everyone who can still start it.

VERIFIER. Steps 12 to 18 are downgraded to medium. Every one of them carries a Lexeme Blade in items or in evidence, and 'Lexeme Blade I', 'II' and 'III' each resolve to nothing -- confirmed against res/items.lua, where 20750/20751/20752 are all named plainly 'Lexeme Blade' -- so stage C drops those entries and steps 12, 14 and 16 are left with no evidence at all while step 18 is left with no requirement. The ladder is still right and the three Superlative runic rings still carry it, but 'the ladder is right and a gate is unmodellable' is the guide's own definition of medium, and the sibling ergon quest Saved by the Bell already marks exactly these rungs medium for exactly this reason. The entries are DOWNGRADED rather than nulled on purpose: stage C turns an all-unresolvable list into no evidence rather than an empty one, so nothing illegal reaches the runtime, and keeping the page's own names is what puts the gap in the quarantine where a human can pin the three ids by hand. Nulling them here would delete that signal and change nothing downstream.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 4: A Trailblazing Pickaxe substitutes for the Pickaxe, an OR that cannot be written beside a required key item, hence items_partial.
  step 9: The page calls it only 'the door behind Yeggha Dolashi' and never names it, so this rung carries no target rather than a guessed one Yeggha Dolashi resolves and stands right there, which is exactly why he is not the target.
  step 12: 'Lexeme Blade I' is the page's name and will not resolve; see the quest note on the three identically named blades.
  step 14: Runic Overflow resolves, so this rung keeps a marker.
  step 18: which is the header's Reward, so by rule it is not evidence, and this last rung carries none.

steps.note: at the Inventors' Coalition. The grid is bullet 18's, since bullet 1 and the header both give none. The sub-bullets are an Idris warning -- you cannot build both ergon weapons at once -- and not a step.
one is enough. Tevigogo, near the Pioneers Coalition, is the page's suggested seller rather than the only source, so he carries the marker while either pickaxe satisfies the step.

from Bivouac #2, north past the Colonization Reive then east into the field of numbing blossoms. There is more than one ??? here -- if nothing happens, find the other. The bush that can block the path at (H-8) is only open 21:00 to 03:00 game time, which the addon cannot see.

Wait for the "Enlightened Endeavor" key item to resonate, then trade. The first dig gives the Numbing blossom seed; keep digging for the Broken rapier hilt, which is what this step is for and so the only evidence. Too slow costs the key item but not the attempt you may try again at once.
back at the Inventors' Coalition.
she starts tracking everything you deposit toward Epeolatry.
cumulative -- you need never hold all 100 at once, so this requirement can read unmet when it is really met. Bullet 8 is the outcome of the trade and not a rung of its own.
keep talking until he mentions the Vial of crimson catalyst.
In from Eastern Adoulin (F-7). Select 'Quiescence'. You must be on Runefencer to enter.

15 minute limit and your subjob is removed. Zurko dual-wields, has the normal sword weapon skills plus Savage Blade and Chant du Cygne, casts only Protect IV, Shell V and Phalanx, and parries often enough that Swipe and Lunge carry your damage; his own Lunge hurts badly with no opposing rune up. The key item is written with its quotes because that is how the resource table names it.
the page's own '(Optional)': a short dialogue pointing you at the Order of Orvail's maester.
A cutscene with Amchuchu, and your base weapon. THE QUEST CLOSES HERE the page says it moves to the completed log at this point and everything below is the rest of the weapon.

Part 1. Bullets 19 and 20 merge: the blade first, then the materials, one visit and one AND-list. Ghastly Stone +1 and +2 are refused, but Ornery Dhole turns them into Obsidian Fragments and 50 of those buy a plain one. 'View materials. (RUN)' shows the running total; deposits are cumulative.
At bivouac #2; Out comes Lexeme Blade II (DMG:228, PDT II -2%).
Part 2, bullets 23 and 24 merged the same way. Verdigris Stone +1 and +2 are refused; 100 Obsidian Fragments each from Ornery Dhole. Cumulative.
at bivouac #2. Out comes Lexeme Blade III (DMG:231, Enmity+10, PDT II -3%).
Part 3, bullets 27 and 28 merged. Wailing Stone +1 and +2 are refused; 200 Obsidian Fragments each. 100 + 500 + 2,500 + 9,999 is the header's 13,099 High-Purity Bayld, and all of it is cumulative.

On top of the barrel beside the Delve NPC at the Inventors Coalition. Out comes Epeolatry Bullets 31 to 33 (Geosuke, then a million gil to Runje for a replacement blade) are a recovery procedure, not a rung, and the page marks that figure unverified itself.
